privacy.privateBadge: Living person — only your family sees them
privacy.privateHelp: Nothing about a living person is ever published. Only members of this family space can see them.
privacy.sensitiveHelp: This is a sensitive fact ({kind}). If the person is living, it stays with whoever recorded it until they give consent.

dates.examplesTitle: Write it the way you know it, for example:

hints.yearSpan: “{from}-{to}” can be read two ways. Write “entre {from} y {to}” if you don't know the exact year, or “de {from} a {to}” if it was a period.
hints.ambiguous: We won't guess this date. Write the month as a word, for example “3 de abril de 1923”.
hints.twoDigitYear: Write the full year: “19{year}” or “18{year}”, not just “{year}”.
hints.monthOver12: Dates are read in the order day, month, year, and there is no month {month}. Write the month as a word, for example “{day} de marzo de 1923”.
hints.weekday: The day of the week does not match the date. Remove it or check the date.
hints.invalid: We could not read this date. Try one of the forms in the examples.

editor.title: Edit {name}
editor.namesLead: As it appears on the birth or baptism record. Other recorded names are kept.
editor.particleHint: Only if there is one: “de”, “de la”, “del”.
editor.nombreUsadoHint: If they used another of their names, for example “Lupe” for “María Guadalupe”.
editor.nicknamesHint: Separate them with commas: “Chucho, el Güero”.

errors.nameRequired: Write at least one given name or surname.
errors.tooLong: A field is too long (120 characters at most; particles, 20).
errors.tooManyNicknames: You can record up to 10 nicknames.

events.title: Events
events.descriptionHint: Optional. For example, the parish or the place.
events.birthNotSaved: The person was saved, but the birth date was not: {hint} You can add it below as a birth event.

relationships.title: Relatives
relationships.kind: What are they to this person?
relationships.statusHint: Civil and religious marriages are recorded as events, with their dates.
relationships.newPersonLead: Write what you know; you can fill in the rest later.
relationships.pickRequired: Choose a person from the list.
relationships.samePerson: A person cannot be their own relative.
relationships.createdWithoutLink: The new person was saved, but the relationship was not: {error}
relationships.confirmRemove: Remove the relationship with {name}? The person stays in the tree; only this link is removed.

picker.label: Search by name
picker.hint: Type at least two letters. Nicknames work too: “Chucho” finds Jesús.

godparents.title: Godparents
godparents.phraseHint: For example: “padrino de anillos” (ring sponsor), “madrina de lazo” (lasso sponsor).

compadrazgo.title: Compadrazgo
compadrazgo.lead: Godparents, godchildren and co-parents (compadres), worked out from the godparents of each sacrament.
compadrazgo.empty: No godparents are recorded yet on the events of this person or their family.
compadrazgo.unavailable: We could not load the compadrazgo: {error}

kinship.title: How are we related?
kinship.lead: Choose two people from the tree and we tell you what one is to the other: “great-uncle”, “co-brother-in-law”, “second cousin”.
kinship.noRelation: We found no recorded relationship between these two people. A link may be missing from the tree.
kinship.swap: See it the other way round

tree.title: {name}'s tree
tree.drawingLabel: {name}'s tree: {count, plural, one {# person} other {# people}}. The same information is in the list below.
tree.listLead: The same information as the drawing, for screen readers and keyboards.
tree.panHint: Drag to move and pinch to zoom. With a keyboard: arrows to move, + and − to zoom.
tree.hiddenChildren: {count, plural, one {and # more person} other {and # more people}}
tree.truncated: This tree is large: we show up to {max} people around the person in the centre.
tree.failed: {count, plural, one {We could not load # relative.} other {We could not load # relatives.}}
tree.emptyAncestors: No parents are recorded for this person yet.
tree.emptyDescendants: No children or partners are recorded for this person yet.

jobs.pollFailed: We could not check progress: {error} We will try again.

import.title: Import a tree (GEDCOM)
import.lead: Bring your tree from another program. People, families and sources are added to this space; nothing already here is deleted.
import.fileHint: .ged files (GEDCOM 7 or 5.5.1) or .gdz files (GEDZIP, with photos), up to 25 MiB.
import.wrongType: The file must end in .ged or .gdz.
import.tooLarge: The file is {size}; the limit is 25 MiB.
import.notAllowed: Only the space's stewards and editors can import.
import.started: We received your file and are reading it; you can stay on this page.
import.countsTitle: What we found in the file
import.createdTitle: What was added to your tree
import.diagnosticsTitle: {count, plural, =0 {No notices} one {# notice} other {# notices}}
import.diagnosticsLead: What we had to adjust or could not read. Nothing is lost: what we do not understand is kept as is.
import.extensionsLead: Data only the source program understands. We keep it so it comes back out when you export.
import.noReport: The import finished, but the server sent no details.
import.openSpace: See the people in this space

export.title: Take everything
export.lead: Your tree is yours. Download all of it whenever you want, in open formats other programs understand.
export.free: Free for every family, always. It does not depend on any plan.

gedzip.name: GEDZIP (GEDCOM 7 with photos)
gedzip.body: Everything in one .gdz file: the tree plus its photos and documents. The most complete way to move to another modern program.

gedcom7.name: GEDCOM 7
gedcom7.body: Just the tree, without photos, in the current standard format. For programs that already read GEDCOM 7.

gedcom551.name: GEDCOM 5.5.1
gedcom551.body: The older format that almost every program reads. Some data is adapted; the report says which.

native_json.name: Complete copy (JSON)
native_json.body: Everything exactly as it is here, with nothing lost. To keep as a backup or to import again.

export.preparing: We are preparing your file. You can stay on this page.
export.expires: The link works until {date}. After that, prepare another download.
export.expired: This link has expired. Prepare another download.
